## Work log

<!-- Chronological, written as you go. What was actually done, why, what it cost.

- **Read Sam's slides through the Slides API** and tallied characters per font. The family is
  Rubik, not "Rubrik": Rubik 400/600 italic for text, Rubik Microbe for headlines, and Dirt,
  Vinyl, Wet Paint, Pixels and Burned for accents. All are free on Google Fonts.
- **Planned [style typography](../plans/2026-10-02_style-typography.plan.md).** Yan chose Rubik
  for both the app UI and comics, and balloons that follow their style live.
- **Built it.** Each style now sets the lettering for every balloon type (family, weight,
  italic, capitals) in a `style_profiles.typography` column.
  - A balloon with no font of its own follows its style.
  - The old Comic Neue and Bangers stamps count as unset, so existing comics move onto Rubik
    with no document migration.
  - The house default is Rubik, with italic capitals for captions, after the slides' narration,
    and Rubik Microbe for SFX.
  - The Inspector font menu has a "Style — …" option; there is a Typography section on the
    style page; the app UI is in Rubik with a Microbe wordmark.
- **Rubik is wider than the system font,** so the editor toolbar clipped at 1440px. Its icon
  buttons now show icons only below 2xl.
- **Tests:** unit 334, integration 34 and e2e 24, all green.
- **Shipped** (7bfcabc): the migration went to production, then Yan ran `vercel deploy --prod`.
- **Checked the live comics in the browser** by measuring text against its box. Production is
  all Rubik. Of 81 balloons, 8 now overflow:
  - **6 speech balloons and captions** (Youngest Delegate p1 ×2, p4 ×2; Year It Snowed p2–p4)
    run 5–35px too tall, because Rubik is wider than Comic Neue.
  - **2 SFX** (BEEP BOOP, FSSSSHH) run about 40px too wide, because Rubik Microbe is much wider
    than Bangers.
  - Waiting on Yan: refit those balloons, or change the defaults.
- **Font menus that preview each font.** Yan wants SFX to choose freely among Rubik Dirt,
  Microbe and the other cuts, picked by eye as in Slides. Built `FontPicker`, a keyboard listbox
  that draws each name in its own face, for the Inspector and the style page.
  - Two fixes along the way: a space typed mid-name had picked the font early, and the
    Inspector's list was wider than its panel and got clipped.
  - **Fixed a test race.** `styles.e2e` and the new typography test both assumed their style was
    first in the team-wide list, so run in parallel they picked each other's. Both now press ↓
    until their own style is checked (`e2e/support/styles.ts`).
  - **Ran the tests in a clean worktree** (HEAD plus only these changes), because the A1-board
    session was editing the same tree. There, `auth`, `collab`, `mcp` and `share` fail on HEAD's
    A1 change (new comics have 16 panels, not 12). Not from this work.
- **Story paneling, *The Youngest Delegate* (Khai's chapter).** Drafted 7-page dialogue, then
  set it aside for paneling. Read the geometry of Sam's slides: an A1 board, a 350 pt header, a
  1684 pt square of comic and a 350 pt footer. At a reading distance of 1–1.5 m the square reads
  like a hand-held comic page, so it holds 7–9 panels on a 4×4 grid and 80–120 words. Proposed 54
  panels over 7 pages, one per Edited Drafts scene. Yan put the story in **Act Two, "Taming
  Currents"**, and pinned the story work until the app supports the board.
- **Planned the [A1 board format](../plans/2026-10-02_a1-board-format.plan.md):** a square grid
  between a header and a footer, comic-wide defaults with per-page overrides, and balloons that
  escape the grid.
- **Built the A1 board** ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_a1-board-format.plan.md)). New comics are
  1000 × 1416 boards: a 4 × 4 grid in the 1000 × 1000 square between a 208-unit header and footer.
  The header and footer have comic-wide defaults that each page can override, in the Inspector
  and over MCP (`set_header_footer`). Balloons already lived on the page, so they cross panel
  borders and the bands with no change. Checked in Chrome against local Supabase: header editing,
  Use on every page, Tab order (header → panels → footer), a caption straddling a border, a
  balloon in the footer, and an A1 `@page` for PDF. That check found new balloons landing on the
  header title; fixed so they start inside the grid. Unit tests: 366.
- **Another session was editing the same checkout** (the font picker for style typography). I
  committed only my own hunks of `Inspector.svelte`, and checked my commits in a clean worktree.
  GitHub had nothing new to pull.

- **Sam's feedback on *The Year It Snowed* and *Visa for a Hilsa*** ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_sam-feedback-snow-hilsa.plan.md)).
  Drafted v2 scripts in `content/drafts/`: Snow now has 5 A1 pages and Hilsa 7, one page per
  scene, plus Hilsa's new prologue.
  - In Snow, Act 2 now teaches three things: a landing board of many indices, with GDP as the old
    single number; weakest-link scoring, with help going to the weakest tier ahead of need; and
    Ya's growth, from napkin to notebook to research.
  - The Hilsa prologue follows Shapla's foremothers (1947, 1971, the drowned delta), with a brass
    pot carried by each generation, and ends on displaced animals.
  - Marcus and Shakil's Monsoon Hilsa ideas go in captions: the Passage Covenant, the NeurOtolith,
    "custodial origin unresolved" as the real reason for 0 taka, and "one season is weather".
  - Waiting on Yan and Sam to confirm the listed inventions before the doc tabs change or the
    comics are rebuilt.
- **Balloon design** ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_balloon-design.plan.md)), from the three
  `speech_bubble-inspo` moodboard photos. Five additions:
  - **Roundness**, from an exact ellipse to a box; tails attach to whatever outline it makes.
  - **Counts** for cloud bumps and shout spikes, plus a spike depth.
  - **Corner anchors**: the balloon is cut off flush by the panel border, which stays whole over
    it, and it follows the corner when the grid changes.
  - **Connected balloons**: a neck that merges the two outlines, or a thin line.
  - **Strikethrough** in balloon text.

  Yan chose the flush trim, and necks as the default with the line as the option. Checking in
  Chrome found two fixes: Inspector edits now re-seat an anchored balloon, and a connector meets
  a clipped balloon where it shows. Unit tests: 405. Open: a neck between balloons in different
  panels crosses the gutter.
- **A QR code to riverbanks.lol in every board footer** ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_footer-qr.plan.md)),
  about 89 mm on A1, with the address under it and a live link in the PDF. It is editable per
  page like the other footer slots. Chrome's BarcodeDetector decoded the rendered code as
  https://riverbanks.lol; a phone scan of a printed board is still to do.

- **Downloaded the images from Sam's slides 1–8** into `riverbanks/paneling-slides/`, which is
  gitignored: 14 files at about 1024 px, the most Slides will serve.
- **The Youngest Delegate v2 panel outline** is written into the *Script: The Youngest Delegate*
  tab, above v1, with a local copy in `content/drafts/`.
  - The layout is 7 A1 boards and 38 panels, one board per Edited Drafts scene. Dialogue comes
    later.
  - The throne room is drawn from the same camera on pages 1, 4 and 6, while the power shifts.
  - Page 3 teaches PREMISE, PROSPER, PESA and KAN; page 5 is split between the General and the
    Financier; the Accord is signed outdoors.
  - Yan: the whole story is in Act Two, "Taming Currents".
  - Yan: the flotel must look like Sam's slides 5–6, a city of pontoon islands around an arched
    hall, not a ship.
  - Then added the dialogue and captions, 37–92 words a page. Lines come from Edited Drafts,
    trimmed; the captions on page 3 teach the four institutions. The tab's v2 section was replaced
    after checking that nobody had edited it in the meantime.
- **Room for lettering in generated panels**
  ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_lettering-room.plan.md)). The blank cream bands in Hilsa 2.3 and
  2.5 came from my own panel prompts ("leave calm, empty space…"). The app now adds a
  room-for-lettering sentence to every panel draft, placed from the balloons already on the
  panel.
  - A test of 8 drafts in a scratch comic showed that naming frames, borders or edges, even to
    forbid them, made the model draw its own inner border. Plain scenery wording ("open sky with
    a few soft clouds") did best.
  - The inner border still appears in some drafts; auto-cropping is a possible next step.
- **SFX rotation** ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_sfx-rotation.plan.md)): −180° to 180°, from the
  Inspector and MCP.

- **Started the A1 comic of *The Youngest Delegate*** (`5a2cdb4a-c822-4fb3-bb5e-5f7d2656a420`),
  built from the v2 script. The art-style test comic is left as it was.
  - Added two places to the house style's cast. **The flotel** is drawn from Sam's slide 6. The
    sheet came out close to his design: an arched hall between two towers, cottages, domed
    pavilions, water pools and turbines. **The throne room of Mua** is the recurring set for pages
    1, 4 and 6. Its first sheet had garbled text, so I redrew it.
  - Page 1 has six panels and eleven balloons, checked in Chrome. I fixed caption overflow: the
    italic capitals run wider than estimated. The brothers' balloons cross the border into the big
    panel's floor.
  - Pages 2–6 are generated, lettered and checked by eye.
    - Redrawn for continuity: 2.4 (no room for Dew's line), 5.2 (the soldier was in red), and 6.4
      and 6.6 (the brothers were off-model).
    - Lettering changes from the script: Dew's line is trimmed to "Taste. The whole river is in
      this bowl."; the fishers caption moves to 5.3; the 1914 Johor line becomes a quoted caption
      on the sepia inset; and the Financier's 6.1 boast sits in the header band.
  - The Gemini prepaid credits ran out before page 7 and were topped up. Page 7 is done: the Accord
    signed outdoors, the crown set aside, and Ismahan in the council circle. Its opening caption
    covers a stray "2030" label the model drew. **All 7 pages are done and checked:** 38 panels.
  - Yan: **the General has no moustache**, and every scene of his must match. I made the cast
    description say clean-shaven with a black crew cut, drew a new sheet and starred it, then
    checked every panel with him at full resolution. I redrew 1.2 (moustache), and 6.4 and 6.6
    (older, greying); the rest were already clean-shaven. In 6.4 the General was hidden behind a
    balloon, so I moved it. Yan was editing the lettering live at the same time, so I changed only
    images and that one balloon's position.
  - Yan named the princes **Tengku Hamzah** (the General) and **Tengku Faris** (the Financier). The
    names are in the cast aliases, the page-1 labels, Edited Drafts' cast list, the script tab and
    the canon file. The story network still shows "The General" and "The Financier".
  - More consistency fixes from Yan's review:
    - **5.5:** redrawn so the PREMISE button is a flat on-screen button, not a real button sticking
      out of the laptop.
    - **4.4 and 4.5:** redrawn as closer shots that match the zoom Yan had set by hand.
    - **The Sultan** always has his short grey beard now.
    - **Hamzah's shirt** is always tucked in with a brown belt, sleeves down; Yan chose this.
    - Both rules are written into the cast descriptions, with a new Hamzah sheet. To match, I redrew
      1.2, 1.4, 4.3 (heads moved below Yan's caption), 4.4 and 5.3.
  - **Wrap-up.**
    - Synced the *Script: The Youngest Delegate* tab and the local draft with the built comic,
      including Yan's live lettering, and fixed three typos in it.
    - Recorded the pinned character looks and the new comic in the canon file.
    - Wrote [the plan](../plans/2026-10-02_youngest-delegate-a1.plan.md) after the fact.
    - Re-synced the story network: Tengku Hamzah and Tengku Faris. The first save failed to copy a
      portrait, with no error message; the retry worked.
- **A1 board v2 ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_board-dimensions-5x4.plan.md)).**
  - Yan's annotated sheet in the moodboard sets new target dimensions. On A1 (594 × 841 mm), the
    comic is 594 × 742.5 mm (5:4) with no side margins, and the header and footer are 49.25 mm
    each.
  - In page units, new boards are now 83 + 1250 + 83. The grid stays 4 × 4, and its cells grow
    taller.
  - Header title and subtitle now share one line. The footer follows the sheet: `{comic}`,
    `{page} / {pages}`, then `RIVERBANKS · SEAPUNK STUDIOS`, then the QR with its address beside it.
  - Old 208-band boards are still recognised as A1.
  - Converted *The Youngest Delegate* without regenerating any art.
    - Each image was re-fitted at the same zoom and focus. Balloons kept their place in their
      panel, and tails follow the art.
    - The half-width panels lose about 8% of the picture on each side. Only panel 6.2 needed a pan.
    - Sam inserted a blank page 2 mid-run, so the later edits were addressed to the shifted pages.
    - The pre-conversion snapshot is in `content/snapshots/`.
- **Header and footer on/off per page ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_band-toggles.plan.md)).**
  - The Inspector's Page section has Header and Footer checkboxes. Off leaves the strip blank
    (Yan's choice) and keeps the text for when it is ticked back on.
  - MCP `set_header_footer` takes `show`.
  - Found while verifying: ⌘Z was ignored whenever a checkbox had focus. Fixed in the shortcut
    handler.
- **The Year It Snowed, polished and built on A1 ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_sam-feedback-snow-hilsa.plan.md)).**

  - New cast place *Dew's restaurant on the Ping*; its sheet is clean.
  - Built comic `YIS` (`cfdcd0d6…`): 5 boards, 22 panels, every page lettered and checked by eye.
  - Redraws: 2.1 (Ya drawn as a man), 2.4 (napkin pyramid on its side), 3.3 (speakers in the
